title: Veterans Pension Care-Cost Adjustments — Medical Deduction Against Countable Income
content:
## Medical deduction in a Veterans Pension care-cost rate adjustment

**Deduction.** The medical deduction is the medical figure — the insurance premiums counted plus the care cost — less the medical threshold, when medical expense reports are on file on the award, and nothing otherwise. The medical threshold is 5 percent of the rate category's basic rate for the medical deduction, rounded to the cent: 872.00 in a no-dependent category (5 percent of 17440) and 1141.90 in a one-dependent category (5 percent of 22838).

**Countable income after the medical deduction** follows the deduction:

| Medical deduction | Compared with countable income | Countable income after the deduction |
|---|---|---|
| positive | smaller | the countable income less the deduction |
| positive | at least as large | none — zero |
| zero or negative, or no medical expense reports on file | — | the countable income whole |

### Cases on both sides (hypothetical, no-dependent category, countable income 9000.00)

| Medical figure | Deduction (figure less 872.00) | Countable income after the deduction |
|---|---|---|
| 872.00 | 0 — not positive | 9000.00 |
| 4872.00 | 4000.00 | 5000.00 |
| 9872.00 | 9000.00 — equal to the income | 0 |
| 12000.00 | 11128.00 | 0 |
| (no medical expense reports on file) | nothing | 9000.00 |
